details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:348-382 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The checkout-ref resolution uses bare `gh api` calls without retry/robust validation, so transient GitHub/API failures or malformed responses can make the job fall back to the default ref or abort instead of preserving the intended baseline ref.
  WHY: Multiple reviewers observed the initial issue-metadata fetch and related branch-ref checks are not wrapped in `gh_retry`, and non-JSON or transient failures can break the subsequent `jq` parsing or silently degrade to the default checkout branch.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:357-357 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The step writes `ISSUE_META_FILE` before validating the `gh api` output, so a non-JSON but non-empty response can poison the cached metadata and prevent the downstream refetch guard from running.
  WHY: Because the file is written first and downstream checks only test for non-empty content, later steps can skip recovery and then fail on `jq` parsing of the corrupted file.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:370-385 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The `prior_pr_baseline_branch` extraction regex fails to match normal issue-body lines that end at the newline, so the preserved baseline branch hint is silently ignored.
  WHY: When the regex does not match, the workflow falls back to `integration/default`, causing implement runs to check out the wrong ref instead of the preserved baseline.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:1240-1255 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: `_rb_valid_repo_relative_path` does not fully enforce its path-safety contract for repo-relative file hints, allowing some malformed or traversal-adjacent values to survive validation.
  WHY: Reviewers flagged both bare `.`/`..` acceptance and `.git/...`-style paths reaching downstream `git ls-tree`, so the validator is incomplete relative to how the values are consumed.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:1268-1273 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: `_rb_push_reissue_baseline_branch` suppresses stderr from `git worktree add` and `git checkout -b`, hiding the underlying setup failure when baseline creation does not succeed.
  WHY: Reviewers agreed the flow degrades safely to redo, but the suppressed diagnostics make root-cause analysis difficult and can waste retries on failures that are not push-related.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:1372-1372 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The caller labels any `_rb_push_reissue_baseline_branch` failure as `baseline_branch_push_failed`, even when the failure happened before the push loop.
  WHY: This misattributes worktree/checkout setup failures as push failures, sending operators to investigate the wrong subsystem.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:1368-1368 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The baseline branch name uses `$(date +%s)`, so two runs for the same PR in the same second can generate the same branch name.
  WHY: That collision makes the second remote push fail non-fast-forward/branch-exists and then degrade to redo after retries.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:1390-1395 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The baseline branch name also relies on second-resolution timestamp uniqueness, creating the same same-second collision risk for concurrent runs.
  WHY: If two runners compute the same `ai/reissue-baseline/...-$(date +%s)` name, one push will fail and eventually fall back to redo after retries.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:1402-1408 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus, minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: When `reissue_mode=spot-fix` has no `new_issue` title/body, the code downgrades to redo without creating a replacement issue, even though `judge_handled=true` is still emitted.
  WHY: That leaves the PR closed with no follow-up issue while downstream orchestration may still assume the reissue happened; one reviewer also noted the lack of explicit test coverage for this edge case.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:1265-1270 | severity=low | confidence=1
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The cleanup trap is set only for `EXIT`, not for termination signals such as `SIGTERM` or `SIGINT`.
  WHY: Runner interruption could skip temporary worktree cleanup, so the trap should cover signal exits as well.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

  WHY: A transient GitHub error or non-JSON response can make `jq -r '.body // ""'` fail under `set -euo pipefail`, terminating the implement job instead of preserving the intended fallback behavior.

  PROBLEM: `_rb_valid_repo_relative_path` does not explicitly reject bare `.` or `..` as valid paths.
  WHY: The validator contract is incomplete because a path like `.` could slip through even though downstream consumers expect repo-relative file paths.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:1268-1270 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `git worktree add` and `git checkout -b` suppress stderr, which hides the underlying git error when baseline push fails.
  WHY: The flow still degrades to redo safely, but the lost diagnostics make debugging much harder.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:1402-1408 | severity=medium | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: There is no explicit test case for the `close_and_reissue` spot-fix path when `new_issue` title/body are missing.
  WHY: This is a coverage gap for an edge case that could regress silently in a future refactor.
